policy: This register tracks open items, not amendments. Blocked decisions are not approved by implementing defaults; later NFL changes never propagate automatically.

items.anchor: 1. Definitions for the analytics terms: role execution, opponent-adjusted difficulty, leverage, replacement baseline, opportunity threshold.
items.next_action: Define statistical analytics in calibration data during Phase 4

items.anchor: 2. Engine content: play catalogue, numeric route landmarks, blocking rules, coverage responsibilities, ball flight, injury and fatigue models.
items.next_action: Build a tested game-action and physics catalogue during Phase 3

items.anchor: 3. Negotiation and market-clearing mechanics; development, aging and retirement curves.
items.next_action: Implement market clearing and aging curves in the character/people layer

items.anchor: 4. Bowl roster repair mechanism when a position shortfall occurs.
items.next_action: Present a deterministic ranked-choice fallback for approval
items.blocker_reason: Bowl shortfall repair rule must be decided before official All-Star selections

items.anchor: 5. The real-time to simulated-time mapping under deterministic pacing (target about 50 hours a season, non-binding).
items.next_action: Calibrate deterministic live-time mapping as a presentation parameter

items.anchor: 6. §19 promises a stable ID on every rule; none are assigned yet, so the changelog uses section references.
items.next_action: Atomize the 158 coarse clauses and attach implementation/test evidence
items.blocker_reason: Every normative rule needs stable, atomic source identity

items.anchor: 7. Tie-game frequency: ties are excluded from records, so the order of overall wins before overall win % matters only when ties occur. Calibrate in simulation so that ties stay highly unlikely.
items.next_action: Measure tie frequency without changing standings treatment

items.anchor: 8. Fill-in parameters inherited from the NFL and not yet confirmed: game-day roster 48/47, two practice-squad elevations a game and three a player a season, four-game injured reserve minimum. The out-of-position penalty belongs with engine content (item 2).
items.next_action: Verify and adopt or replace the 2026 NFL-derived provisional numbers
items.blocker_reason: Emergency game-day, elevation and IR defaults must be explicitly frozen

items.anchor: 9. Standings assumptions to confirm: higher strength of schedule and strength of victory rank higher (NFL default); a club with no decisions has a win % of 0; the seeded draw is the last resort and is rerun from a season-and-scope seed.
items.next_action: Lock higher SOS/SOV, zero win percentage for no-decisions and deterministic final draw—or amend explicitly
items.blocker_reason: Standings SOS/SOV, no-decision and seeded draw defaults must be explicitly frozen

items.anchor: 10. Calibrate the pre-cut cap count (§0) once the market exists: it is adapted from the NFL's top 51 of a 90-player camp roster, and the ratio does not carry over exactly. (The rookie reserve, §11, is built and replaces the open question about rookie room.)
items.next_action: Test top-69 economic viability and approve the pre-cut cap figure
items.blocker_reason: Top-69 preseason cap treatment is normative; calibrate and approve before founding

items.anchor: 11. Floor removal relies on the sentiment and recall mechanism pricing poor spending and poor results; its inputs are unbuilt (people layer). Payroll spread across clubs is a fairness-band candidate.
items.next_action: Implement measured fan sentiment and recall response to low spending

items.anchor: 12. Emergency cap borrowing (owner proposal): deferred. The viability invariant is built so that no legal roster is ever unreachable; revisit only if a real jam appears once the market exists.
items.next_action: Keep emergency cap borrowing deferred until real viability failure exists

items.anchor: 13. Exile-return loop: a club exiled as last place returns the next year as seed 5 with a lottery pick in slots 1-8; whether this traps weak clubs in a cycle, and whether extra picks for exiled clubs would help or would reward losing, must be measured with the real engine (parity profiles, Phase 4).
items.next_action: Measure exile-return feedback without rewarding intentional losing
Approve precise offseason windows and remove stand-in dates
items.blocker_reason: Provisional offseason windows must become a fixed calendar before founding

items.anchor: 15. Character attributes, their means and the age curve are placeholders until the engine (Phase 3) says which attributes it uses and how; the attribute list and every distribution are data in `data/characters/` and may change. Overall ratings are not yet comparable across positions (a calibration job for Phase 3/4).
items.next_action: Calibrate attribute lists/distributions and age curves when game roles exist

items.anchor: 16. Appearance: the creation look is immutable; whether and how a character visibly ages is decided in presentation (Phase 7), by redrawing from the stored look.
items.next_action: Derive visible aging from immutable creation look in viewer implementation

items.anchor: 17. Leader pools and hiring (four willing candidates per role, §13) use the same creator and the four-year pool rule; the hiring market itself is people-layer work (Phase 5).
items.next_action: Build four-candidate role pools and hiring market within existing creator rules

items.anchor: 18. Jersey numbers: none open. The same-club re-signing reclaim and lowest-open assignment are the builder's defaults (change on request).
items.next_action: Retain existing approved jersey-number builder defaults
